The Court made the following:
ORDER:
This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of the India seeking the following reliefs:-
"to issue a writ order or direction more particulariy one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus deciaring the action of th th the respondents, more particulariy the 4 and 5 respondents in trying to lay CC (Cement Concrete) road on the petitioners private patta land situated in Sy.No.191-3 admeasuring Ac.0-33 % cents of Vellatur Village,
Pendlamarri Mandal, Kadapa, YSR Kadapa District without acquiring the land as per Land Acquisition Act, as illegal,arbitrary and unconstitutional and in violation of the procedure contemplated in Right to Fair Compensation and NV,J Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and consequently direct the aforesaid respondents not to lay any road on the petitioners private patta land without acquiring the land such in accordance order or with the Land Acquisition Act and pass orders... '' learned 2. Heard

sentences.text:
the learned counsel for the petitioners, the Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings and Sri M. Sudheer, learned Standing counsel appearing for the respondent No.6.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the absolute owners and possessors of the extent admeasuring Ac.0-33 Ya cents in Sy.No.191-3 at Vellatur Village,
Pendlamarri Mandal, Kadapa, YSR Kadapa District, having acquired the subject property through a Registered Sale Deed document dated 20.04.2023.

After acquisition of the subject property through a sale deed, the petitioners got mutated as Pattadars and possessors of the subject property into the revenue records and they were issued Pattadar Passbooks as well as other revenue well as records which substantiate the ownership of the petitioners and as possession.
While so the respondent authorities without issuing any notice and without following the due process of law as contemplated under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition.
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013), are trying to dispossess the petitioner for laying a CC Road.
Hence, the present Writ Petition.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings furnished the written instructions issued by the 4^^ respondent c^; NV,J dated O8411.2024, wherein it is stated that the respondent Nos. 2 to 5 are not taking any steps for laying any road through the subject land of the petitioners' as alleged by them.
4. Learned Standing counsel appearing for the 6 respondent also submits that the respondent also not taking any steps for laying any Road in the subject land as alleged by the petitioners.
It is only a mere apprehension of the petitioners.

5. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned Government Pleader and the learned Standing Counsel, this Court is of the opinion that the writ petition can be dispose of, by directing the respondents not to interfere with the possession of the petitioners and if they intend to lay any road through the subject property of the petitioners as claimed by the petitioners, they shall follow due process of law as required under law.
6. With these observations and directions, this Writ Petition stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.
7. Consequently, Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
